description:
FILED s414 (Opus) probing the &-mention family of gen_funcall_form (#387).
The HALF that was a plain bug is FIXED in the same commit: p-defined-fh
resolved its own way (a raw `gethash sym *p-filehandles*`) instead of through
p-get-stream, so it missed the standard handles â they are registered under
the :pcl symbols while generated code in a user package passes that package's
own same-named symbol â and `defined STDIN` read FALSE.  Guard row in
Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t.  What follows is the RESIDUE, which needs a
decision, not a patch.

PROBED (perl 5.40.3):
  perl -e 'print defined(NOPE) ? 1 : 0'                 # 1
  perl -Mstrict -e 'print defined(STDIN) ? 1 : 0'       # COMPILE ERROR:
                                                        #   Bareword "STDIN" not
                                                        #   allowed while "strict
                                                        #   subs" in use
  perl -e 'open(FH,"<","/etc/hostname"); close FH;
           print defined(FH) ? 1 : 0'                   # 1
So `defined BAREWORD` in perl is NOT an openness test at all: without strict
the bareword is the STRING "NOPE"/"FH" and `defined` of a string is always
true; under strict it is a compile error; and when a sub of that name is
declared, the bareword is a CALL and perl tests its return value.

PCL implements "is the handle open" (ExprToCL's `defined` arm emits
(p-defined-fh 'NAME) for a /^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$/ bareword).  That agrees with
perl for an OPEN handle and diverges for a closed or never-opened one:
  defined NOPE   perl 1, PCL 0
  defined FH     (after close)  perl 1, PCL 0

DECISION NEEDED, not obvious either way: matching perl means the arm always
answers true, which is useless but correct, and must still not fire when a
sub of that name exists (perl would CALL it).  Principle 1 (match Perl
semantics exactly) points at doing it; the counter-argument is that no real
program asks `defined FH` expecting "true always", so the divergence may be
worth keeping as a documented one in docs/not-supported.md.  Whichever way it
goes, the sub-exists case must be handled first â that is the shape a real
program hits.
subject: `defined BAREWORD` answers "is this handle open", perl answers "is the string defined" â a never-opened or closed bareword reads false in PCL, true in perl (and under strict perl refuses the bareword outright)
